items.title: Why shopping on your phone can make you second-guess a purchase
items.summary: You find the product you want on your phone. You compare prices, read reviews and weigh the options. Then, just before tapping "Buy," you hesitate: Maybe I should look at this again on my computer.

items.title: Recycling food waste could return essential minerals to crops, food and animal feed
items.summary: While vast populations face malnourishment and starvation, mountains of food are wasted in affluent countries, which leads to poor food system efficiency, depleted resources, micronutrient losses through ultraprocessed food and environmental degradation.

items.title: Smoke-affected hops have greatest impact on beer when added after fermentation, study finds
items.summary: Smoke-affected hops can alter a beer's taste and aroma, but their impact depends on how many are used and when the hops are added during brewing, new research from Oregon State University shows.

items.title: Could astronomers be closing in on a hidden planet beyond Neptune?
items.summary: If a hidden planet really does exist beyond Neptune, astronomers have identified how it may look and act to explain the mysterious goings-on in the distant reaches of our solar system.

items.title: Public protests can reduce sexual violence

The surprising findings challenge a longstanding evolutionary theory and suggest that viruses may have hidden capabilities far beyond simply infecting cells.

items.title: UK digging new reservoirs to fight persistent droughts
items.summary: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the U.K. is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades.
